accuracy.evidence: Checked against NC Year 5 Forces (unsupported objects fall towards the Earth because of gravity acting between the Earth and the object), NGSS 5-PS2-1 (Earth's gravitational force is directed down, i.e. towards the centre) and the BBC Bitesize KS2 gravity guide. g is given as about 9.8 N/kg, rounded to 10 N/kg for ages 9–11, and every forcemeter reading (1, 5, 10, 20 N) is shown with ≈. The equal-fall claim is limited to objects of the same size and shape or to no air; the Apollo 15 hammer-and-feather drop (David Scott, August 1971) is dated correctly. The lab's race uses one acceleration for both balls and a low terminal speed only for the feather in air.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented gravity misconceptions (Allen, Misconceptions in Primary Science; Driver et al., Making Sense of Secondary Science; Nussbaum's Earth-concept studies): no forces on a resting object, heavier falls faster, air pushes things down, 'down' as the bottom of the page so people fall off the far side of the globe, and mass in kg confused with weight in N. Each is a prediction option, a refusal message or a tagged challenge answer.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagdrop has five scenes no other lab has: support-force arrows that vanish when the table, string or hand is removed and the object then accelerates to the floor; timed drop races (heavy/light, feather with and without air in a dashed vacuum tube); a globe where people can be dragged round the rim before dropping balls along the radius; and a spring forcemeter that stretches in proportion to the hung mass. flaggapforce sorts contact versus non-contact forces and flagfdiag draws arrows; neither removes supports or times falls. Shingle gate passed.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers the support force by seeing two equal arrows on a still book, then sees only the red gravity arrow left when they take the table away; the ball race lands both balls on the same frame before the text says so; the feather race shows air as the only difference; the globe makes the bottom person's ball fall upward on the page but towards the centre; doubling the hung mass doubles the reading. Water running downhill is covered in the kid text and a mastery item.

predictions.evidence: Five predictions with tempting wrong options: 'no, because it is not moving', 'stays in the air', 'the heavy one, by a lot', 'down the page, off into space' and '10 N: gravity is the same for all'. Each is disproved by doing its task.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven rotating questions with tags air, want, still, heavy, light, nograv, map, unit and kg; each wrong answer names the slip, e.g. 'Gravity still pulls the book. The table pushes up just as hard, so the forces balance' and 'Kilograms measure mass. Weight is a force, so it is measured in newtons.'

readability.evidence: Kid text FK grade 3.2 (family target ≤ 5), key idea 5.7, adult 7.7 (≤ 10). Gravity, unsupported, balance, weight, newton and forcemeter are each explained in one short sentence where they first appear; the kid text avoids 'acceleration' and says 'gets faster' instead.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passed with no filler phrases and under 12% overlap with any lesson, including 622 Contact & Non-Contact Forces, 589 Forces Vocabulary and 569 Measuring mass and weight. Kid paragraphs: what gravity is with jumping and rain as examples, support and falling, heavy versus light, which way is down and weight. Adult: standards, the physics, five named mistakes, the lab.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 screenshots of every scene after Show me in dark and light: the three stations fit at 390 px with force labels on opaque chips so the table leg and the hand do not cover them; arrows are hidden once an object lands so 'landed' sits clear; the race header carries the race count so the lane labels stay clear; the forcemeter stretch is capped so a 2 kg mass stays above the feedback pill; feedback wraps onto two lines on a pill instead of shrinking.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: Forces on the book/lamp/ball, Take away the table/string/hand, three Race buttons, Drop the top/right/bottom/left ball and Hang 100 g/500 g/1 kg/2 kg. The canvas aria-label repeats each feedback line. walk.cjs: axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13; reduced motion shortens the Show me timings.
